w: The largest performing-arts and arts-education center on Cleveland's West Shore — a nonprofit founded in 1931 (as Lakewood Little Theatre) that entertains and educates 65,000+ people a year across two stages on a 3.5-acre Detroit Ave campus. Professional theater, galleries, and classes; documented by the Encyclopedia of Cleveland History and listed by TourismOhio.
sources: Encyclopedia of Cleveland History (CWRU) — Lakewood Little Theatre / Beck Center (est. 1931)
Ohio.org — Beck Center for the Arts, Lakewood

w: A 1921 neo-classical movie palace that opened with the Gordon Square Arcade and shuttered in 1985 amid the neighborhood's decline — then fully restored and reopened in 2009 as the anchor of the Gordon Square Arts District's revival, now a Cleveland Cinemas first-run-and-indie house. Documented by Cleveland Historical and Heritage Ohio.
sources: Cleveland Historical — Capitol Theatre (1921, Gordon Square Arcade), restored 2009

w: The Gordon Square / Detroit-Shoreway theater complex that has been the home of experimental and socially engaged theater in Cleveland since James Levin founded it in 1981 — a driving force in the arts-district revival. Covered by Cleveland Historical and Cleveland Scene.
sources: Cleveland Historical — Cleveland Public Theatre (founded 1981), Gordon Square
Cleveland Scene — Cleveland Public Theatre, Detroit-Shoreway

n: Rocky River Reservation & Fort Hill Stairs
w: A Cleveland Metroparks jewel of the Emerald Necklace winding along the Rocky River — over five miles of trails to river's edge, wetlands, ponds and ancient Native American earthworks, plus the Fort Hill Stairs (155 steps rising 90 ft to a bluff-top view). The Rocky River Nature Center displays the prehistoric fish Dunkleosteus and the kid-favorite HideAway Hollow oak.
sources: Cleveland Metroparks — Rocky River Reservation & Nature Center; Fort Hill Stairs
Cleveland Scene — Rocky River Nature Center, Western Suburbs

address: Lake Rd at Wolf Rd, Bay Village, OH 44140
w: A ~100-acre Cleveland Metroparks lakefront reservation in Bay Village with a swimming beach on Lake Erie, three miles of trails through beach-forest-meadow habitats, and the landmark 1927 Huntington water tower with a play space and snack spot. Home to two Metroparks affiliates (Lake Erie Nature & Science Center and BAYarts).
sources: OhioDNR / Ohio.org — Huntington Reservation, Lake Erie Birding Trail

w: A free, family-favorite nature and science center in Huntington Reservation with a planetarium, live-wildlife exhibits and a wildlife-rehabilitation program on the Lake Erie shore. Covered by Ohio Magazine and Destination Cleveland.
sources: Ohio Magazine — Lake Erie Nature & Science Center, Bay Village
Destination Cleveland — Lake Erie Nature & Science Center (free)

w: A lakeside arts campus in Huntington Reservation — galleries, artist studios, a gift shop and year-round classes for adults and children, plus a summer art festival. A Cleveland Metroparks affiliate listed by Destination Cleveland.
sources: Cleveland Metroparks affiliate — BAYarts, Huntington Reservation
Destination Cleveland — BAYarts, Bay Village arts campus

w: One of the oldest municipally owned arts parks in the U.S., conceived in 1938 by Heights drama teacher Dr. Dina Rees Evans and Mayor Frank C. Cain — the covered 2,782-seat Evans Amphitheater, the Alma Theater, the Feinberg gallery, and the July Cain Park Arts Festival, a nationally top-rated juried outdoor art fair. Entrances at Lee Rd and Superior Park Dr.
sources: cleveland.com — Cain Park Arts Festival, top-rated outdoor arts festival

w: Cleveland's premier arthouse cinema and the anchor of the Cedar Lee district — open since 1925 and now a six-screen Cleveland Cinemas house for indie, foreign and documentary films, famous for its monthly midnight 'Rocky Horror Picture Show.'
sources: Cleveland Scene — Cedar Lee Theatre, indie/foreign arthouse (Rocky Horror midnight)
cleveland.com — Cedar Lee, historic Cleveland Heights cinema (1925)

w: An eclectic, pedestrian-friendly Cleveland Heights arts-and-shopping strip of vintage shops, indie boutiques, bookstores and diverse restaurants — often called Cleveland's answer to Greenwich Village, and the longtime countercultural heart of the east side.
sources: Destination Cleveland — Coventry Village, Cleveland Heights
cleveland.com — Coventry Village, eclectic arts & shopping district

w: A sandstone farmhouse built in 1834 by Scottish immigrant John Honam — over its life a post office, shoe-repair, doctor's office and barbershop — moved into Lakewood Park in 1952 by the Lakewood Historical Society and now a museum of Rockport Township and Lakewood history. Documented by Clio and Ohio Traveler; open limited hours (Wed & Sun).
sources: Clio — Oldest Stone House (built 1834, John Honam; Lakewood Historical Society)
Ohio Traveler — Old Stone House Museum, Lakewood Park
